name: EXTEND
fullName: Thrombolysis Guided by Perfusion Imaging up to 9 Hours after Onset
teachingPoint: Supports perfusion-mismatch IVT in 4.5-9 h window when EVT not indicated.

name: EPITHET
finding: Primary endpoint not met: infarct growth non-significantly lower with alteplase; reperfusion significantly more common
teachingPoint: Conceptual basis for later mismatch-based late-window trials.

name: ECASS4-EXTEND
fullName: Extending the Time Window for IV Thrombolysis Using MRI-based Selection
population: n=119, ≥18 (upper limit needs confirmation), NIHSS 4-26, 4.5-9 h or unknown onset
finding: Favored alteplase numerically; not statistically significant after early termination
teachingPoint: Adds to the late-window mismatch evidence base; not independently practice-changing.

name: TIMELESS
fullName: Tenecteplase for Stroke at 4.5 to 24 Hours with Perfusion-Imaging Selection
finding: Favored TNK numerically; primary endpoint did not reach significance overall
teachingPoint: Cautionary: late-window TNK alone (with EVT permitted) did not meet its primary endpoint.

name: TRACE-III
fullName: Tenecteplase for Ischemic Stroke 4.5-24 Hours without Thrombectomy
teachingPoint: Supports the tested perfusion-selected late-window TNK strategy where EVT was unavailable, within the trial selection and bleeding trade-off.

name: HOPE
fullName: Alteplase for Acute Ischemic Stroke at 4.5 to 24 Hours: The HOPE Randomized Clinical Trial
teachingPoint: Positive evidence for the tested perfusion-selected late-window alteplase strategy in patients with no initial EVT plan, including eligible patients who declined EVT. Selective, not evidence that all participants were EVT-ineligible.

name: EXPECTS
fullName: Alteplase for Posterior Circulation Ischemic Stroke at 4.5 to 24 Hours
population: n=234, adults, NIHSS median 3 (mainly mild), 4.5-24 h
teachingPoint: Supports late-window thrombolysis for selected mild posterior-circulation stroke without perfusion mismatch requirement; remains emerging, not routine.

name: CHABLIS-T II
fullName: Tenecteplase Thrombolysis for Stroke up to 24 Hours After Onset With Perfusion Imaging Selection (CHABLIS-T II)
finding: 33.3% (37/111) vs 10.8% (12/113); no significant difference in 90-day clinical outcomes
teachingPoint: Adds to the mixed late-window TNK evidence base; reinforces that reperfusion gains have not consistently translated to clinical benefit.

name: TRACE-5
fullName: Tenecteplase versus standard medical treatment for basilar artery occlusion within 24 h (TRACE-5): a multicentre, prospective, randomised, open-label, blinded-endpoint, superiority, phase 3 trial
population: n=452, adults ≥18; mean 66.4 y (SD 11.2); 321 (71%) male, 131 (29%) female, NIHSS any — no NIHSS threshold in the registered eligibility (randomisation balanced on NIHSS <10 vs ≥10), within 24 h of stroke onset or last known well
finding: POSITIVE: 83/221 (38%) with tenecteplase vs 66/231 (29%) with standard medical treatment
teachingPoint: In Chinese patients with basilar artery occlusion and pc-ASPECTS ≥6 treated within 24 h, intravenous tenecteplase (with thrombectomy at clinician discretion) improved the 90-day rate of mRS 0-1 or return to baseline versus standard medical treatment (38% vs 29%), without a demonstrated difference in symptomatic haemorrhage or death. It provides dedicated randomised support for thrombolysis in BAO up to 24 h. It does not establish benefit of tenecteplase as a bridge before thrombectomy beyond 4.5 h (ATTENTION LATE was neutral), awaits replication outside China, and postdates the AHA/ASA 2026 and ESO/ESMINT 2024 guidance, so it remains emerging evidence that guidelines do not yet endorse.

name: OPTION (TNK)
fullName: Tenecteplase for Acute Non-Large Vessel Occlusion 4.5 to 24 Hours After Ischemic Stroke: The OPTION Randomized Clinical Trial
population: n=570, ≥18 (median 68, IQR 59-75); 196 (34.6%) female, NIHSS 6-25, or 4-5 with a disabling deficit, 4.5-24 h from last seen well (wake-up and unwitnessed onset eligible)
finding: Favoured tenecteplase: 123/282 (43.6%) vs 97/284 (34.2%) with standard medical treatment
teachingPoint: Adds a single positive RCT for perfusion-selected IV tenecteplase at 4.5-24 h in non-LVO stroke when EVT is not planned: excellent outcome 43.6% vs 34.2%, at the cost of symptomatic ICH 2.8% vs 0%. Emerging, selective and consult-dependent — it post-dates the 2026 AHA/ASA guideline, is not yet replicated outside China, and should not be generalised to patients without a CTP target mismatch or to those proceeding to thrombectomy.
